short: STN-only adaptation (M03) closes 75-76% of the retraining gap, not the 88% the abstract states; untested against lower-layer adaptation; dev-set MSE only (M12 behind).
position: The paper [@toth2023adaptation] changes speaker and session adaptation (M03) by retraining only a learned affine transform of the input image (a spatial transformer, STN) placed before the usual CNN regressor (M06). The design is new for articulatory-to-speech adaptation (Appendix), but M03 is standard: the obvious baseline, the same group's lower-layer adaptation [@gosztolya2020applying], is never run. M06 is standard: in matched conditions the STN moves development MSE by at most 0.021 (session 5: 0.504 without, 0.483 with; Table 1; inference). M12 is behind: one regression error on an unnamed split, without the held-out passage and listening test of the prior study. The abstract overstates: it credits "adapting just the STN module" with 88%, which in Table 2 is the average of the "STN + out" column and a share of the no-adaptation-to-full-retraining gap, not an MSE reduction; the STN alone closes 75–76%.
